title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model-call accounting: one shared initial generation per pair (720) plus one repair-stage call (total model_calls_used = 721). These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, provider-call accounting clarification, artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher‑order safety/policy constraints. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports advocate such workflow-centred mitigations [1]–[3], but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a controlled paired study to measure the aggregate detection-rate difference contributed uniquely by an automated sandboxed-emulation stage when the same initial generated candidate is analyzed by both conditions.

Our preregistered research question was: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (3) a concise, artifact-supported explanation for a near-zero marginal effect in this constrained regime; (4) reproducibility pointers and prescriptive boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent surveys and architectural reports document the trend of combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1]. These works emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional (syntactic parsing, command-ordering/workflow constraints, invariants, and dynamic runtime properties) and that different V&V primitives address different dimensions. Tool-focused case studies trace the evolution and limits of static verifiers and show why some systems layer an emulator after static validation to exercise temporal behaviors and state transitions [2]. Prototype integrations report heterogeneous gains from emulation: in some regimes static verification already captures most hazards, while in others emulation uncovers runtime or environment-specific side effects that static rules miss [3].

Positioning. Our paired, shared_initial_candidate design isolates only downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or permitted repair invocations) and therefore complements prior work that conflates generation variability with downstream verification benefits.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures), multiplicity treatment for exploratory comparisons, contamination controls, and an explicit shared_initial_candidate enforcement: for each pair exactly one sampled initial candidate is produced and presented identically to both downstream conditions.

Task bank, vendors, and topology templates. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 task family. The bank spans three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds. In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720, per the preregistration.

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses); the client did not set an explicit temperature (recorded as null in the archived model configuration). For each pair the pipeline obtained exactly one shared initial candidate (one provider call) and delivered that identical candidate to both the baseline and guarded downstream conditions. This isolates guarded-stage signals from generation variability.

Baseline validator and guarded emulation. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performs deterministic rule-based checks: vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints, protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs the same validator and then, regardless of the validator outcome, executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology template and executes the normalized CLI commands on vendor‑abstracted virtual devices. Emulation translates runtime observations (interface transitions, concurrent-interface states, MTU/VLAN application effects, observable reachability consequences) into runtime-observation rules that can trigger guarded detections not encoded in the static validator.

Provider-call accounting and audit-field clarification. The preregistered execution recorded model call events in a provider_call_audit structure that reports (among other fields) hosted_model_call_event_count, stage_counts, and condition_counts. These fields caused reviewer confusion because condition_counts can appear asymmetric even when complete_pair_count = 720. The artifact-grounded explanation is straightforward and recorded in the execution manifest/deterministic reconciliation: stage_counts label calls by pipeline stage (e.g., "shared_initial_generation": 720, "repair": 1). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics each pair requires exactly one shared initial generation; that single shared initial call is attributed to the shared stage in stage_counts (and to a "shared" bucket in condition_counts) even though its generated candidate is evaluated by both baseline and guarded downstream conditions. Any additional model calls (for example repair-stage invocations) are separately counted and—if they occur—are attributed to the guarded stage. Thus an audit showing hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 with stage_counts shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1 means: 720 shared initial calls (one per pair) plus one repair invocation executed only in the guarded pipeline. This explains the apparent asymmetry: the shared initial generation is a single model call per pair that serves both conditions, whereas guarded-only calls (repairs) are counted separately. The canonical execution manifest in the archived bundle records these fields and the mapping between model-call events and pair identifiers; auditors can verify the mapping there.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inference (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are reproduced verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts.

Repair and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single n10 discordant pair must be attributable to either (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not codified as a validator violation, or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage model invocation. The archived raw_results.jsonl contains the per-episode records (including validator_trace and any repair_provider_trace) that map the discordant pair_id to the recorded repair-event; auditors can inspect that canonical record in the archived bundle to see the exact linkage. No irrecoverable technical exclusions occurred; complete_pair_count = 720.

Representative diagnostics. Representative scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show normalized_configuration, validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count = 0 for most items; these traces illustrate that the validator matched the curated task patterns and that emulation largely corroborated validator findings in this bank.
sections.discussion:
Why the guarded-stage aggregate benefit was negligible. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the near-zero marginal effect.

Validator ceiling and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator explicitly encoded the syntactic and semantic checks exercised by the curated tasks (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Representative validator_trace objects show parsed_command_count ≈ required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for most shared_initial candidates. The baseline success rate of 719/720 leaves essentially no headroom for emulation to add detections in this constrained regime.

Curated inclusion reduces adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items were parser-validated and generated deterministically; this inclusion policy intentionally limited inputs to scenarios the validator could analyze, underrepresenting runtime-only faults that emulation reveals in more diverse or adversarial settings. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation confirm zero irrecoverable parser exclusions.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. Reusing the identical sampled initial candidate isolates downstream guarded effects, but it also removes any benefit that could arise from independent re-generation in the guarded condition (e.g., re-prompting before validation). Provider_call_audit shows only a single repair invocation across 720 pairs; that single repair accounts for the lone guarded-only detection.

Operational implications. For operator pipelines that enforce strong parser validation and maintain a high-coverage static validator aligned to expected intent patterns, adding an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may offer negligible incremental detection benefit. This does not render sandboxing unnecessary: in noisy, adversarial, or production-like regimes (uncurated natural-language intents, broader vendor diversity, long-lived multi-step state) emulation can detect dynamic behaviors and side effects static rules cannot anticipate. Practically, operators should: (i) invest in richer static validators for high-throughput low-latency workflows; (ii) apply guarded sandboxing selectively to high-risk changes; (iii) use adversarial/fuzzing task banks to reveal validator gaps. Our archived artifacts include representative traces suitable as seed cases for such adversarial design.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call auditing records a single repair-stage invocation corresponding to the unique guarded-only detection; shared_initial_candidate semantics ensure that this discordance is traceable in the archived per-episode records. We interpret the result as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding driven by validator ceiling effects and curated task selection. Extensions to adversarial task banks, expanded vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation are required to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value. The archived execution manifest and per-episode artifacts provide the canonical bundle for independent verification.

Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration was frozen before execution). Immutable initial master-prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. For full per-file provenance, model-call audit, and the canonical execution artifacts (execution manifest, raw_results, analysis artifacts, and logs) consult the archived execution manifest included in the submission artifact bundle; that manifest is the authoritative pointer to the archived run.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
